$comment: P40 lane L (D-ML7-2.3 parallel-copy resolution x D-ML7-2.5 outgoing-argument pre-coloring): the GPR counterpart of `arg_move_cycle`, which witnesses only an 8-element FP rotation that fills the FP argument pool exactly. Four shapes the FP example leaves unwitnessed at runtime, on the side where the outgoing-argument pre-coloring makes cycles ROUTINE rather than accidental: S1 a 2-cycle (the swap `t2(b,a)` -- no ordering of two moves is correct, so a caller-saved scratch of the class must carry one source); S2 a 3-cycle, proving the break is not special-cased to length 2; S3 a cycle PLUS AN ACYCLIC TAIL, so the resolver must both order the acyclic move and break the cycle in ONE move set -- and must not choose the tail's destination as its scratch; S4 NINE arguments with a leading swap, more than any shipped ABI passes in registers (SysV 6, Win64 4, AAPCS64 8), so the register cycle and the stack overflow compose and the stack stores must read their sources before any register move clobbers one. Each callee weights its parameters by distinct powers of two, so no permutation error can cancel out, and each shape carries its OWN exit code so a failure names the shape. Inputs derive from a volatile global so the release arm cannot fold the calls away. RED-ON-DISABLE: emit the arg moves in order instead of breaking the cycle and every shape reads a clobbered source -- a SILENT wrong answer, hence the per-shape exit codes. => 42.
